correctness.rationale: For all even q=2d, the midpoint disjoint-rich-interval argument bounds the index by 2iota(H)+1 and exactly characterizes the extra arch by remainder letter-set coverage under the fixed-point-free involution. Surjective-word ordinary generating functions count unique greedy arches and incomplete remainders; complement-pair occupancy gives binom(d,j-d)2^(q-j). Minimum length qk follows from constant patterns, and every length-qk universal word is a permutation-block concatenation; the involution symmetry forces mirrored blocks and the central 2^d d! invariant permutations. A standalone independent pattern-checker exhaustively checked 32199 symmetric hosts and 2647 literal cases, with 24 generating-function profiles and 10 shortest host cases. The computational range is only a supplementary finite verification.

originality.rationale: The result supplies the involution-orbit remainder criterion and complete rational enumeration for fixed-point-free Watson-Crick palindromes. Barker et al., arXiv:2003.04629v1, Proposition 15 proves a related ordinary-palindrome index formula but does not incorporate complement pairing; Proposition 18 treats morphic letter permutation without reversal. Mahalingam et al., arXiv:2008.00255v1 studies theta conjugacy but not scattered subsequence universality. Schnoebelen and Veron, arXiv:2304.11932v1 gives general arch-jumping algorithms, not the particular bivariate formulas. Residual unindexed-equivalence risk remains.
residual_risks: The general method resembles published arch-index reasoning; an unlocated source may already enumerate the Watson-Crick specialization.

value.rationale: Involution-symmetric words model Watson-Crick reverse-complement structure. The natural nonregular family admits a complete exact bivariate universality-index distribution and all-parametric optimal-length/multiplicity classification. The central cover condition transitions from the ordinary palindrome missing-letter requirement to full occupancy of all complement pairs, yielding odd-index universality even for even-length symmetric hosts. This structural and enumerative classification is not a cheap normalization check or isolated small numerical gain; the proof and all-parameter recurrence apply for every even alphabet size and all k.
